transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
NVIDIA's board has reinstated Jensen Wong
as the company's CEO.
Wong resigned earlier this month due to multiple affairs,
in particular, one with a possible Chinese spy.
NPR's Stephen Besaha reports President Trump said
rehiring Wong would be the best move for the United States.
NVIDIA is at the center of the artificial intelligence industry,
not only because it provides advanced computer chips needed to develop AI,
but also because it acts like a bank providing loans for other AI companies.
NVIDIA's stock has been plummeting ever since Wong's ouster two weeks ago.
NVIDIA's board sent out a press release saying senior levels of the U.S. government
convinced them Wong is not a national security risk.
That said, the board will continue supporting an independent investigation
into whether Wong was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.
After the reinstatement, President Trump wrote on social media
congratulating Wong and called him a great patriot.
Stephen Besaha, NPR News.
Additionally, on Truth Social, Trump says the U.S. has no reason to believe
Wong's return poses a national security risk.
He also writes the government does not possess evidence
that Wong has engaged in any unlawful conduct,
but Trump writes NVIDIA should continue an internal investigation
of its compliance with U.S. export controls.
In eastern Iowa, the U.S. Army says it will carry out the controlled detonation
of nearly five tons of unstable explosives on Wednesday.
Those explosives contain lead.
Elijah Billingham with Iowa Public Radio reports.
The Army says the lead azide has become unstable and must be disposed of.
An earlier planned controlled detonation had been delayed at the last minute
after public outcry and a lawsuit from environmental groups.
Michael Schmidt from the Iowa Environmental Council
said federal officials didn't give local leaders enough time
to notify residents of the potential of lead-laden dust across the region.
That would have allowed them to make informed decisions
to protect the health and safety of our communities.
But the Army said federal rules allow the Army to continue
if there's imminent danger to the public.
It says cold weather puts the already unstable chemical
at too high a risk of uncontrolled explosion,
so it will do the controlled detonation right before the holiday.
For NPR News, I'm Eliza Billingham in Iowa City.
Nearly 200 countries remain at an impasse over fossil fuels,
and NPR's Rachel Waldhoat says the parties walked away
from COP 31 climate summit in Turkey over the weekend
without an agreement on money.
Developing countries want more help dealing with climate change.
They point out that they've contributed very little to global warming,
but are often dealing with some of the worst impacts.
And wealthy countries who are most responsible for climate change
agreed to provide funding as part of the Paris Climate Agreement.
And, of course, one big wealthy country
that wasn't at the climate talks is the U.S.
The Trump administration has withdrawn
from the international climate negotiation.
NPR's Rachel Waldhoat's reporting.
This is NPR News.
British authorities say nearly 90 people were medically evaluated
after getting sick from an unknown substance release
at rapper Don Tolliver's concert in Manchester last night.
The incident prompted the evacuation
of about 12,000 people inside the arena.
Generations of Sesame Street fans
might remember an episode or two about kindness.
-It's nice to be kind. -Oh, that's catchy.
-Thank you. -Well, the Sesame Workshop
is out with a new survey that finds families of young children say
their kids are kind, even as they overwhelmingly see the world
as a very unkind place.
Here's NPR's Corey Turner.
-The education nonprofit behind Sesame Street
has twice surveyed American families about kindness
in 2016 and now a decade later.
And the differences are striking.
This national sample of caregivers of kids ages 3 to 8
saw a big increase in families who say kindness
is just not a priority for most people.
And they gave Americans a pretty middling rating
for kindness, 2.8 out of 5.
But compared to a decade ago, kids earned higher marks
for kindness and resilience,
and they were less likely to be considered anxious.
Caregivers themselves were also much more likely in 2026
to say they value empathy in their kids over manners.
Corey Turner, NPR News.
-Crowdstrike says it is acquiring Zscaler
in an all-stock deal worth nearly $44 billion.
The deal combines two of the biggest names
in the cybersecurity industry.
This is "NPR News."
-This message comes from Build,
where members earn points on every housing payment.

and ask the neighborhood concierge
about perks near your home.

topics.text: NVIDIA's board reinstates CEO Jensen Huang after resignation over affairs and spy concerns
Trump calls Huang a great patriot and says no national security risk found
Trump urges NVIDIA to continue internal investigation of export control compliance
Army plans controlled detonation of nearly five tons of unstable lead azide in eastern Iowa
Iowa environmental groups criticize federal officials for insufficient notice before detonation
COP31 climate summit in Turkey ends without agreement on climate funding
Nearly 90 people evaluated after unknown substance release at Don Toliver concert in Manchester
Sesame Workshop survey finds families see kids as kind but the world as unkind
CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler in all-stock deal worth nearly $44 billion
